title: Knowledge_level
summary:
The knowledge level is a concept in artificial intelligence introduced by Allen Newell in 1982. At the knowledge level, an agent is described as having a set of objectives, a set of possible actions, and a body of knowledge. The agent takes actions based on knowledge it possesses, in an attempt to reach specific goals, choosing actions according to the principle of rationality.

Knowledge at this level is characterised as a notion of competence, being a potential to generate actions. Knowledge is completely independent of representation and implementation questions. The knowledge level provides a way to rationalize an agents behavior by focusing on what the agent knows and what its goals are, as a logical abstraction separate from details of implementation.

Beneath the knowledge level resides the symbol level. Whereas the knowledge level is world oriented, concerning the environment in which the agent operates, the symbol level is system oriented, including the mechanisms the agent has available to operate. The knowledge level rationalizes the agents behavior, while the symbol level mechanizes the agents behavior.

For example, in a computer program, the knowledge level consists of the information contained in its data structures that it uses to perform certain actions. The symbol level consists of the programs algorithms, the data structures themselves, and so on. Allen Newell saw minds and computers as knowledge systems that may be understood in terms of the content of their beliefs and goals, with behavior predicted and explained by assuming that the system pursues goals in light of its beliefs.
